title: Elijah “stretched himself upon the child”; the soul “came into him again” — Brenton’s Greek says he breathed on the child and the child cried out
summary: KJV 1 Kings 17:21 has Elijah stretch himself on the child three times, and 17:22 has the child’s soul come into him again so that he revived. The Hebrew prints וַיִּתְמֹדֵד and וַיֶּחִי; Brenton’s Greek prints ἐνεφύσησε, “breathed on”, at 17:21 and at 17:22 “And it was so; and the child cried out”.

[And he breathed on the child three times, and called on the Lord … let the soul of this child turn back into him]. title: The false witnesses say Naboth “did blaspheme God and the king” — Brenton’s Greek prints the verb of blessing

title: Ahab rises and goes down to the vineyard — Brenton’s Greek adds that he first tore his clothes and put on sackcloth
summary: In the KJV of 1 Kings 21:16 Ahab hears that Naboth is dead and goes straight down to the vineyard. Brenton’s Greek (its chapter 20) prints that he tore his clothes and put on sackcloth, and only after that went down.
text: KJV 1 Kings 21:16: “And it came to pass, when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, that Ahab rose up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.” Hebrew (WLC) 21:16: וַיְהִ֛י כִּשְׁמֹ֥עַ אַחְאָ֖ב כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת נָבֹ֑ות וַיָּ֣קָם אַחְאָ֗ב לָרֶ֛דֶת אֶל־כֶּ֛רֶם נָבֹ֥ות הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֖י לְרִשְׁתֹּֽו׃ ס Brenton’s Greek 20:16: Καὶ ἐγένετο ὡς ἤκουσεν Ἀχαὰβ ὅτι τέθνηκε Ναβουθαὶ ὁ Ἰεζραηλίτης, καὶ διέῤῥηξε τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, καὶ περιεβάλετο σάκκον· καὶ ἐγένετο μετὰ ταῦτα, καὶ ἀνέστη καὶ κατέβη Ἀχαὰβ εἰς τὸν ἀμπελῶνα Ναβουθαὶ τοῦ Ἰεζραηλίτου κληρονομῆσαι αὐτόν. [and it came to pass, when Achaab heard that Naboth the Jezreelite was dead, he tore his garments and put on sackcloth; and it came to pass after this, he rose up and went down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to take possession of it] Fetched from https://ebible.org/eng-kjv/1KI21.htm, https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/11/21/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/1KI20.htm.
reasoning: The Hebrew edition quoted has Ahab hear of Naboth’s death and rise to go down. The Greek printed at the same verse puts an act of mourning, tearing his clothes and putting on sackcloth, on hearing the news. The KJV reports tearing and sackcloth at 21:27, after Elijah’s word, as the act that follows the judgment. The Greek at 21:16 reports tearing and sackcloth at an earlier moment, on hearing of Naboth’s death.
scope: T applies at 1 Kings 21:16 only. The record does not compare 21:27, which both texts print, and does not say that Ahab did not mourn twice. It states only that the Greek has the act at 21:16 and the Hebrew and KJV do not. It does not say what the Greek translators or later copyists intended. This compares the wording of the texts quoted. It does not show which wording is original. The book is a history written in prose; the comparison is of what the texts print, not of why the writer worded it so. The Hebrew quoted is the Westminster Leningrad Codex digital text. A digital named edition is not proof that every manuscript agrees; other Hebrew manuscripts were not examined. The Greek quoted is Brenton’s printed edition of the Septuagint, an ancient Greek translation tradition of the Old Testament. It is not a critical apparatus and does not show that all Greek witnesses agree or which reading is original, and the record does not claim the Greek is a mistranslation of the Hebrew. English in square brackets is the researcher’s plain rendering, not a KJV quotation and not a lexicon entry.
